feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles: it presents a clear niche, solid progression, and relevant public-sector impact. Writing is polished and professional overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond web scale, and slightly overstuffed with overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary define a focused value proposition in digital platforms, governance, content operations, and AI-enabled experiences.  
- Strong career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within NACo show trust, growth, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good use of scale indicators: examples like 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and enterprise tools strengthen impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well but need clearer results (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings, campaign performance).  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “social, and multimedia” vs. “web, email, social and video”); “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—prefer “French (A2, learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and foreground the strongest differentiators: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and public-sector scale.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, outcome-oriented language such as “leading” or “delivering.”
- Consider adding one concrete scale marker from recent roles (for example, 10,000+ pages or 3.5M annual page views) to increase impact.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds and scales analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories slightly more distinctive will improve scan value and reduce repetition.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Replace broad items with more specific, higher-signal terms: “Content governance and editorial operations” and “Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Content governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and structured content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space is tight, drop one lower-priority item such as “Multi-channel communications operations,” which is already well established elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeats the header and recent projects almost verbatim.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent NACo roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinctive and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Emphasize outcomes where possible: e.g., improved policy-content discovery, supported campaign growth, extended conference engagement, or expanded recurring advocacy reach.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [project] to [goal/outcome].”
- Consider tightening wording: “bill-level AI chat” may read more clearly as “AI chat at the bill level” or “bill-specific AI chat.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series overlap with the current consultant and NACo experience bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider foregrounding it or making the others more outcome-focused to avoid repetition.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles by emphasizing advisory scope, platform delivery, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, and content operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 outcome-led bullets; start with strong verbs like “Advised,” “Built,” “Led,” “Delivered.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/pages, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow improvements, search accuracy, time saved, or engagement gains.
- Example rewrite:
- Advise NACo on digital strategy, web governance, and content operations for enterprise communications platforms.
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing resource toolkits.
- Improved communications workflows, analytics, and cross-channel publishing systems to support coordinated web, email, social, and multimedia execution.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance/usability/operational best practices” overlaps with the 2022–2024 director role; keep this higher-level and consulting-focused.
- Microsite and AI search details also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same examples verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and the bullets emphasized outcomes, team/operational scope, and what changed under your leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget strategy for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add outcome language where possible: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy programming, events and recurring multimedia series.”
- Rephrase channel/analytics bullets to show decisions/results: “Expanded analytics across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving leadership reporting and channel optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” and recurring video/programming overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization and infrastructure.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears in adjacent NACo roles; avoid repeating “strengthened coordination/workflows” unless tied to a specific measurable change.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, repeatability, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to stress scope and operational ownership: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: newsletters, advocacy video, editorial planning, publishing workflows.
- Add outcomes where possible: open/click rates, newsletter growth, video cadence/views, turnaround time, stakeholder adoption, or workflow efficiency.
- Possible version:
- Managed daily digital operations across web, email, social and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.
- Owned four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing a repeatable policy communications channel.
- Improved cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social and video” is too similar to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; keep focus here on scaling/operationalizing it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct strengths rather than repeating broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-value wording tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications systems leadership
- Public-sector stakeholder communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Governance and usability standards” if you want stronger differentiation from other sections.
- Keep wording noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing leadership traits with execution tasks.
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise web strategy for 10,000+ page, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is already well covered in multiple NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. This topline item should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms most supported by recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder for recency/fit: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, workflow automation, and API integrations; move older/secondary platforms later.
- Replace the long list with grouped phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • AI-enabled search experiences • API integrations and workflow automation • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages • Airtable-based systems”
- Consider dropping one lower-signal item like “jQuery” or “Airtable systems” if space is tight; they are better supported in Technical + IT.
- If you want more impact, use outcome-oriented wording: “Drupal modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Platform/tool specifics are also duplicated in Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization” rather than just product names.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure for 10,000+ page sites” or “reporting for enterprise web modernization.”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” for sharper, more standard wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current content duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- Avoid listing every tool here if they already appear in Technical + IT; keep this section more strategic and senior-level.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and production scope rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to better match seniority: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**

- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- Studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera workflow management
- Virtual event and advocacy content delivery

- “Livestreaming” / “livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies and Technical + IT; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Video production and editing” is too basic given your Director-level profile and repeats evidence already shown in multiple NACo roles.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is the strongest, most recent platform in the CV, lead with it and add light context or proficiency framing.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding a qualifier to show depth, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular content, microsites)** if your format allows short parenthetical context.
- If this section should stay tool-only, tighten the title to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner scanning.
- If space permits, replace **GitHub Pages** with a more impactful platform/tool only if you’ve used another CMS more substantially in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the platform list in only one place.
- Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint already appear elsewhere, so this entry should stay concise rather than repeat capability claims.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to capability-based phrasing: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., implementations supporting Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, or workflow automation.
- Order by strongest/specialized tools first: JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • HTML/CSS • jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may fit better under Analytics/Optimization if that section needs more specificity.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and reads like a generic software list. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills, so it should emphasize systems actually used to drive operations.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to improve clarity and seniority: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” so the heading better matches the content.
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana; move lower-signal tools later or cut one if space is tight.
- If accurate, add a light qualifier in the section intro elsewhere, e.g., “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating those exact phrases multiple times.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if collaboration platforms are important to target roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength from recent roles: enterprise email operations and member engagement platforms. It should read as a capability cluster, not just a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and order by likely relevance/scale: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth without repeating work history: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations and audience engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and credibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding outcomes here unless tied to platform implementation/admin.
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely repeats the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo Director bullet about expanding analytics infrastructure. Make it sharper by emphasizing methods/capabilities rather than re-listing the same tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Measurement & Optimization**
- Replace with a tighter mix of tools + applied capabilities, e.g.: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • SEO analysis • Experimentation**
- Swap vague terms like **Dashboarding** for stronger phrasing such as **Executive reporting** or **Performance measurement**
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to outcomes instead of here (e.g., reporting for 3.5M annual page views, improved decision-making, cross-channel visibility)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly duplicative of **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the detailed tool list here and shortening/removing the topline version.
- **A/B testing** may overstate depth unless supported by a work-experience bullet with a concrete example.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer outcomes if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 concrete outputs with scale: “Supported a major website refresh” could become “helped deliver a website refresh for [X-page/site]” and “produced livestreams and weekly video updates reaching [audience/frequency].”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” if accurate.
- Consider a sharper version: “Produced livestreams, weekly video updates and other digital content while standardizing workflows and supporting cross-channel publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” repeats the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the capability.
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with multiple later roles; frame it as initial setup rather than ongoing leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content advanced advocacy or member engagement.
- Consider dropping “organizational” and “contributed to,” which weaken ownership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Podcast/multimedia work overlaps with later video and digital production roles; keep this entry focused on firsts, research support, and early content innovation.
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing if later roles already show stronger ownership and scale.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only, with concise labels and no broad capability statements already proven elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as tool-focused: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator**
- Replace broad phrases with more specific technical terms if truly needed: **Livestream production systems** instead of “Livestream studio workflows”
- Consider adding proficiency/context only if defensible and recent, e.g. **broadcast-quality video editing**, **audio post-production**
- If space allows, group for readability: **Video/Audio:** Premiere Pro, Audition | **Design:** Photoshop, Illustrator

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” duplicates stronger evidence in Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Director of Digital Media bullets.
- “Podcast production” is already covered in older work experience; keep it only if still a current, differentiating capability.
